findings.title: Cache is not re-checked after taking the write lock, so a waiting request re-reads the manifest and can overwrite a valid cache with nil and return an error
findings.description:
The fast path reads `entryPointAssetsCache` under `RLock` (lines 41-43), releases the lock, and then calls `Lock()` unconditionally (line 48). Another goroutine can populate the cache (line 69) in that window. The waiting goroutine does not re-check the cache after acquiring the lock. It runs the full manifest read again (lines 51-67).

If that second read fails, for example because the manifest is being rewritten during a deploy, `readWebAssetsFromFile` returns `(nil, err)`. Line 69 then stores `nil` into the global, and line 70 returns the error. A request that could have been served from the valid value stored a moment earlier gets an error, and the valid cache is discarded until another request recomputes it.

The pre-change code had the same overwrite on this interleaving. The new lock is where the re-check belongs, because without it the lock only serializes redundant recomputes. The fix is the standard double-checked pattern: after `Lock()`, if `cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil`, return the cached value.

I checked the rest of the change and found no other behavior defects:
- The three callers (`pkg/api/index.go:82`, `pkg/api/frontendsettings.go:62`, `pkg/middleware/recovery.go:141`) only read the returned pointer.
- `SetContentDeliveryURL` is only called on `result` before it is published (line 64). Published values are not mutated afterwards.
- `ContentDeliveryPrefix` and `GetContentDeliveryURL` do not call back into `GetWebAssets`, so there is no re-entrant lock.
- `defer Unlock` covers panics, including the recovery middleware path.
- The CDN branch is unreachable, since `cdn := ""` is always empty.

structured_findings.summary: Cache is not re-checked after taking the write lock, so a waiting request re-reads the manifest and can overwrite a valid cache with nil and return an error
